```{r setup, include=TRUE}
# Code chunk settings (ensure code display)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo = TRUE,       # Code chunk settings
  warning = TRUE,   # Hide warnings (optional)）
  message = TRUE,   # Hide package loading messages (optional)
  fig.cap = ""       # Figure title (can be customized)
)

# Load required packages
library(tidyverse)
library(scales)
library(patchwork)

# 1. Load and Prepare Data
industry_data <- read_csv("expenditure_by_industry.csv")
payment_data <- read_csv("expenditure_by_payment_type.csv")

# Check basic structure
glimpse(industry_data)
glimpse(payment_data)

# 2 Data Sorting
## 2.1 Convert Industry Expenditure Data from Wide to Long Format
industry_long <- industry_data %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = starts_with("cost_"), 
    names_to = "Industry", 
    values_to = "Expenditure"
  ) %>%
  mutate(Industry = str_replace(Industry, "cost_", ""))
## 2.2 Convert Payment Type Data from Wide to Long Format
payment_long <- payment_data %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = starts_with("percent_"),
    names_to = "Payment_Type",
    values_to = "Percent"
  ) %>%
  mutate(Payment_Type = str_replace(Payment_Type, "percent_", ""))
## 2.3 Merge Two Long Tables
full_data <- industry_long %>%
  inner_join(payment_long, by = "response_id", relationship = "many-to-many")
## 2.4 Calculate Weighted Expenditure
full_data <- full_data %>%
  mutate(Weighted_Expenditure = Expenditure * Percent)
# 3. Summarize and Analyze
## 3.1 Total Expenditure by Industry and Payment Method
summary_data <- full_data %>%
  group_by(Industry, Payment_Type) %>%
  summarise(Total_Expenditure = sum(Weighted_Expenditure, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  ungroup()
## 3.2 Total Expenditure by Industry
industry_summary <- summary_data %>%
  group_by(Industry) %>%
  summarise(Industry_Expenditure = sum(Total_Expenditure))
## 3.3 Total Expenditure by Payment Method
payment_summary <- summary_data %>%
  group_by(Payment_Type) %>%
  summarise(Payment_Expenditure = sum(Total_Expenditure))

# 4. Visualizations
## 4.1 Grouped Industry Expenditures (Stacked Bar Chart by Payment Method)
payment_summary <- summary_data %>%
  group_by(Payment_Type) %>%
  summarise(Payment_Expenditure = sum(Total_Expenditure, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(
    Percent = Payment_Expenditure / sum(Payment_Expenditure),
    Payment_Label = paste0(Payment_Type, " (", scales::percent(Percent, accuracy = 0.1), ")")
  )
summary_data <- summary_data %>%
  left_join(payment_summary %>% select(Payment_Type, Payment_Label), by = "Payment_Type")

p1 <- ggplot(summary_data, aes(x = reorder(Industry, Total_Expenditure, sum),
                               y = Total_Expenditure, fill = Payment_Label)) +
  geom_col() +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(title = "Industry Consumption Expenditure 
       (by Payment Method)",
       x = "Industry",
       y = "Total Expenditure",
       fill = "Payment Type") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = dollar_format()) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom",
        plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold"))
p1

## 4.2 Proportion of Payment Methods (Pie Chart)


p2 <- payment_summary %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = "", y = Percent, fill = Payment_Label)) +
  geom_col(width = 1, color = "white") +
  coord_polar(theta = "y") +
  geom_text(aes(label = scales::percent(Percent, accuracy = 0.1)),
            position = position_stack(vjust = 0.5), size = 4) +  # <-- 添加比例标签
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set3") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
  labs(title = "Overall Proportion of Payment Methods") +
  theme_void(base_size = 14) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom",
        plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold"))
p2
# 5 Summary of Consumption Habits Insights

## 5.1 Industry Expenditure
#   The sectors with the highest expenditure are accommodation, eating_out,
### and transport.

## 5.2 Payment Method Preferences
### 5.2.1 Credit card (creditcardatpos) remains the primary payment method, 
### especially in high-value industries (e.g., accommodation, shopping).  
### 5.2.2 Digital payment has grown rapidly in fast-moving consumer goods (FMCG)
### sectors (e.g., food_drink, transport), reflecting the demand for convenient 
### payments.  
### 5.2.3 Cash (cashatpos) usage is gradually declining, but it still accounts 
### for a higher proportion in specific industries such as local_transport.

## 5.3 Industry-Payment Method Linkages
### 5.3.1 The food_drink industry has the highest proportion of digital payments.
### 5.3.2 The accommodation and tourism industry relies far more on credit cards
### than other payment methods.
### 5.3.3 Expenditures in education and healthcare still favor traditional 
### payment methods.

# 6 Recommendations
## 6.1 Promote the development of digital payment channels, especially in the 
### food & drink and transport industries.
## 6.2 Expand credit card partnership programs, such as cashback for large 
### purchases and installment services, targeting customers in premium 
### industries.
## 6.3 Improve the cash payment experience for specific groups who prefer cash 
### (e.g., elderly individuals, small-value transactions).
